plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches, still bare of leaves, break into fragrant blossoms of blush pink, white and deep rose. The flowers often open while frost and sometimes snow linger, so they have long stood for resilience and the first hint of spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late January to March, usually peaking in mid-February to early March in warmer parts of Japan
plants.location: Japan, including Mito, Atami and Kyoto
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms were celebrated in Japan before cherry blossoms became the national favorite. The fruit is pickled as umeboshi and steeped in liqueur as umeshu.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family looks like a crown. Its showy pink bracts surround a center of silky, pale tips. Blooms stand on tough, leathery-leaved shrubs in the fynbos shrublands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late winter to early summer, with flowering at different times depending on the region and the plant. Some blooms may appear in February.
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its flower heads can reach about 30 cm across, and its fire-adapted shrubs resprout after wildfires.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs carry rosette-like blooms in red, pink and white against dark, polished leaves. In mild winter climates, they brighten gardens when little else is in flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, with many varieties at peak in February in mild climates
plants.location: Gardens in the southeastern United States, Japan and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant that gives us tea. Camellia japonica is grown for its flowers, and it has been cultivated in East Asia for centuries.
